name: Springdale · Zion
tagline: A canyon base, with Bryce within reach
summary: Use Springdale for Zion and add Bryce as a separate driving day or overnight. Select hikes for your ability and current conditions rather than treating every viewpoint as an easy stop.
seasonNote: Summer canyon heat can be severe; winter brings ice. Narrows access depends on water and flash-flood conditions.
arrival: Fly to LAS or SGU, then drive or book a transfer to Springdale.
gettingAround: Use town and park shuttles when operating; the main canyon scenic road then restricts private cars. A car is useful for Bryce.
cashTip: Most operators accept cards. Daily budget excludes car hire, fuel and park admission/pass; add them separately. 2026 park rule: eligible non-US visitors aged 16+ pay an additional USD 100 at designated parks unless covered by a valid qualifying pass. The nonresident annual pass is USD 250. Verify party coverage; never assume USD 35 covers all visitors.
foodTip: Pack water and trail food; buy a proper meal in Springdale rather than relying on trail services.
buyTip: Choose outdoor essentials and locally made craft; leave natural objects in the park.
baseArea: Springdale within reach of a town shuttle stop.

items.name: Zion Canyon & Riverside Walk
items.summary: The shuttle-accessed canyon and riverside path are an accessible introduction to Zion.
items.expect: Shuttle queues, changing trail access and a long day outdoors.
items.tip: Use the official shuttle schedule; Riverside Walk is separate from wading into the Narrows.
items.priceNote: No separate trail fee; base park vehicle admission is up to USD 35, plus applicable nonresident fees. A valid pass may cover admission.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: The canyon walls and Virgin River are accessible without an exposed ridge climb.
The paved Riverside Walk makes a useful first introduction to the inner canyon.
visitFlow: Use the official shuttle to the appropriate stop.
Walk the paved route and turn around before entering the river unless separately prepared.
items.tradeoffs: Shuttle queues, changing trail access and a long day outdoors.

items.name: The Narrows, bottom-up option
items.summary: Walk upstream between canyon walls when conditions permit.
items.expect: Uneven riverbed, cold water and flash-flood exposure; not a casual paved walk.
items.tip: Check same-day NPS water/closure advice. Rent suitable gear; turn back early and never enter on a closure.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate for optional equipment rental; park admission separate. Bottom-up access has different permit rules from top-down routes.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: The route enters a slot-like canyon between high sandstone walls.
Walking in the river makes the experience different from a conventional dry trail.
visitFlow: Check same-day NPS closures and water conditions.
Enter only when conditions and equipment suit, then turn around with ample time.
items.tradeoffs: Uneven riverbed, cold water and flash-flood exposure; not a casual paved walk.

items.name: Angels Landing permit hike
items.summary: A famous exposed ridge with dramatic canyon views.
items.expect: Strenuous ascent and severe exposure; a permit is required for the chain section.
items.tip: Only attempt if comfortable with the conditions and exposure. Scout Lookout is a different turnaround option.
items.priceNote: Planning permit-fee allowance; lottery application and per-person charges differ. Park admission is additional.

review.note: Indexed visitor-rating snapshot; check live reviews for changes.

whyVisit: The ridge gives a dramatic view along Zion Canyon.
The exposed chain section is a distinct challenge beyond the uphill approach.
visitFlow: Secure the required permit and assess the conditions honestly.
Turn around at Scout Lookout if the final exposure does not suit you.
items.tradeoffs: Strenuous ascent and severe exposure; a permit is required for the chain section.

items.name: Canyon Overlook Trail
items.summary: A shorter trail reaches an expansive canyon viewpoint near the tunnel.
items.expect: Limited roadside parking, steps and exposed edges.
items.tip: Check road and trail access; do not improvise parking on unsafe shoulders.
items.priceNote: Included after paying park admission or using a valid pass.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: A relatively short trail reaches a broad view above the canyon.
It offers a different angle from the valley-floor shuttle route.
visitFlow: Use a safe legal parking space and check the open trail.
Follow the marked path carefully to the overlook and return.
items.tradeoffs: Limited roadside parking, steps and exposed edges.

items.tip: Stay overnight near Bryce if you want sunrise and a longer hike; check ice and trail closures.
items.priceNote: Separate park admission: base private-vehicle fee up to USD 35 plus applicable nonresident charges; qualifying pass may cover it.

dayClusters.label: Zion orientation and Riverside Walk
dayClusters.note: Prepare food before entering the park and use the shuttle when operating. Start with the canyon and Riverside Walk; wading into the Narrows is a separate activity.

dayClusters.label: The Narrows, if conditions allow
dayClusters.note: Give the river walk its own day and check same-day water, weather and closure information. Replace it with a lower-risk open trail or rest if conditions are unsuitable.

dayClusters.label: East Zion viewpoint and town downtime
dayClusters.note: Use the shorter viewpoint walk, safe parking and a relaxed return to Springdale. This lighter day is useful between longer hikes and driving days.

dayClusters.label: Bryce as an onward park day
dayClusters.note: Reserve a full day for the separate park. If travelling onward across Utah, consider staying near Bryce rather than driving back to Springdale; check route, lodging, cold and trail conditions.

dayClusters.label: Alternative exposed permit hike
dayClusters.note: Use only with the required permit, suitable weather and comfort with severe exposure. It is an alternative to another demanding hiking day or an extra day, not an automatic addition to the Narrows.
